correctness.rationale: For any graph involution, the geometric fixed set of its flag complex is PL homeomorphic to the clique complex of the compatible complete orbits, proved directly by invariant barycentric coordinates. The transposed-addable-corner description of nontrivial orbits is proved diagrammatically. For each integer 1 to 22, an exhaustive independent generator of all partitions, transfer edges, orbits and clique faces validates every ordered codimension-one free-face pair in the embedded certificate. The survivors are graphs whose connected-component counts and cycle ranks give integral homotopy. Separate mod-two rank computations agree; no mod-two-only inference is used. Published ambient sphere-wedge homotopy and finite simplicial Lefschetz give the trace identity, with value -1 exactly at the first negative case n=22 within range. Certified code and certificate filenames are verify.py and certificate.json; limits beyond size 22 explicit.

originality.rationale: Strongest same-object sources were inspected at the level of their precise conclusions. Existing conjugation and axial results concern fixed vertices, not all points fixed in the geometric realization; existing full homotopy theorem concerns nonequivariant type; existing tables ordinary Euler/clique counts. No inspected source implies a fixed-orbit flag model with complete fixed-space homotopy up to n=22 or the sharp loop and negative-trace thresholds. Search incompleteness and not fully accessible synthesis are genuine risks.

value.rationale: The symmetry-fixed realization is a natural new topological object prompted by the actual recent literature on conjugation and equivariant partition-graph models. Its infinite-size exact orbit description and the sharp first nonzero integral H1 at n=18 distinguish new 1-dimensional topology invisible to the ambient 2-sphere wedge and graph-level self-conjugate axis. First negative equivariant trace at n=22 is a natural representation-theoretic transition. The exhaustive free-face collapses supply actual integral homotopy, not just computable numerical trivia; a full all-size classification is not claimed.
